title: RT by @PanteraCapital: 总结一下我们的核心观点： 我们认为纯机器人模型公司显然已经进入商品化的阶段，这也意味着纯模型实验室高估值已经到达了拐点。它们要么通过自己掌握硬件来垂直整合整个技术栈，要么彻底转向前线部署模式，把部署环节握在自己手里。 Fable 5.2 和 Astra 6 的出现，基本意味着通用 LLM 已经可以取代所谓的 system 2；而当这些模型用来写代码去控制机器时，还能继续下沉到 system 1，接管传统机器人栈里的动作规划环节。只要推理长度和所需算力能随时间持续优化，专注于 pre-training 的纯 VLA 实验室追逐通用机器人智能，最终会被彻底淘汰。 有意思的是，我们认为价值最终会沉淀到部署层。从软件的角度看，也就是市场所说的 system 0。而其中的关键在于：持续收集后训练数据，会实质性地提升软件对硬件的控制能力，也让部署本身变得更高效、更好。 至于硬件，我们的观点比较反直觉的是，它反而会成为瓶颈。虽然这一层的利润率大概率会被竞争压低，但这不等于硬件没有价值。公司必须自己掌握硬件，才能完全释放软件的能力。这意味着要自研、自产硬件，确保后训练所优化的一切，都能真正落到硬件层上。

name: Mark Jeffrey
title: RT by @markjeffrey: NYT has responded to my post by claiming that I’m “spreading conspiracy theories.” But which of us is the one trafficking in unsubstantiated allegations? Recent coverage (including CNN, which I QT’d) shows: — The intelligence community has not established conclusive evidence that Alice Huang knowingly acted as a spy or funneled information to Beijing. — There is internal disagreement about the strength of the evidence and whether she was recruited by the MSS. — Attorney General Todd Blanche has said on the record that the Justice Department, he, and FBI Director Patel have reached no conclusions about “who she is or is not.” — Some officials at ODNI and CIA have indicated the “Chinese spy” label is not fully accurate or is “over-torqued” based on the available intercepts and collection. — Incoming House Intelligence Chairman Jim Himes, a Democrat, said it was still unclear whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy immediately after he was briefed. NYT’s stories (which have alleged “Chinese spy” dozens of times) have relied exclusively on anonymous officials. No official has gone on the record affirming it as established fact, and the more recent reporting reflects greater caution and disagreement inside the government. So when I point out that the spy narrative is unconfirmed and increasingly contested, that is not a conspiracy theory. It’s a growing body of evidence that indicts the NYT’s reporting.

name: Tim
title: RT by @tm0klc: “just use a foundation model” they said. so we benchmarked 10 of them against Manako on a real forecourt damage clip. same full 1280x720 frames, same class prompts (person, car, fuel dispenser, fuel nozzle), no crops, no zoom. the hard class is the nozzle/hose. small, thin, occluded, and the thing that actually gets damaged. - Grounding DINO labelled a bin as a fuel nozzle. - Florence-2 labelled the canopy pole as one. - OWL-ViT, YOLOE and YOLO-World got the dispenser at best, never the nozzle. - RF-DETR doesn’t have the class. - Gemma 4 E2B described the scene, boxed the pump, and returned no incident time. the only open model that localised the nozzle was full SAM3. 3.45 GB, 0.2-1 FPS on a Jetson Orin Nano. Manako (3 specialists - 29.5 MB), 3-6 FPS on the same Jetson, tracked the nozzle at 5 FPS and fired a live equipment_damage event on the hose drop at 10.3s. 117x smaller than the only model that could keep up. open-vocab models are great at the classes the internet photographs a lot. operations live in the long tail: nozzles, hoses, cabinets, the small parts that break. that’s where specialised detectors win, and it’s why we built Manako the way we did.
